# The Origin of Thunder

Long ago, when the world was young, the Sky had no voice. It watched silently as humans below celebrated, mourned, and told stories around their fires. The Sky grew lonely, yearning to join their conversations.

One day, the Sky asked the Sun for help. "Give me your voice," pleaded the Sky. But the Sun said, "My voice is light itself. If I give it to you, the world will freeze in darkness."

Next, the Sky approached the Wind. "Lend me your voice," it begged. The Wind whispered, "My voice is the gentle breeze that cools foreheads and carries seeds. Without it, nothing would grow."

Finally, the Sky met the Mountain, oldest of all earthly things. "Wise Mountain," said the Sky, "how can I speak to the humans below?"

The Mountain rumbled thoughtfully, then broke off a piece of its stone heart. "Take this," said the Mountain. "When you roll it across your vast halls, you will have a voice."

The Sky took the stone and rolled it joyfully. The sound boomed and echoed—thunder was born.

Now, whenever thunder rolls across the heavens, it is the Sky speaking, telling its own stories to the world below.
